name: Bouquet
tldr: 💐 often stands in for flowers you wish you could send, especially for support, congratulations, and family warmth.

contextMeanings.meaning: It can simply refer to an actual bouquet or a gift of flowers.
It works as a shortcut for offering warm wishes when no physical flowers will be delivered.
contextMeanings.example: get well soon 💐 thinking of you

contextMeanings.meaning: It can add romance to an anniversary or shared celebration, though it may feel overly formal in a casual relationship.
It can offer professional sympathy in a get-well message, but it may seem too soft for a coworker’s wedding.
contextMeanings.example: hope you're back on your feet soon 💐

platformNotes.note: Apple’s full-color design makes the bouquet easy to recognize and keeps a wedding message warm. In family threads, it can represent flowers sent in emoji form.
WhatsApp uses its own emoji artwork, though its bouquet looks relatively close to Apple’s. Older family-group members often understand 💐 more readily than a complicated wedding emoji stack.
Slack’s professional setting makes 💐 feel ceremonial or slightly too soft in many channels. For a coworker’s wedding, 🎉 alone is usually the safer choice.
Twitter uses its own emoji set, and public wedding posts often rely on the familiar combination of 💐, 💍, and 🥂. A public post remains a poor place for a private get-well gesture.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z recognizes 💐 as a standard part of wedding vocabulary and the soft-warm way to congratulate a couple. It is usually reserved for a clear occasion rather than dropped into an ordinary chat.
Millennials parse 💐 easily, but some may find layered emoji stacks performative. In close relationships, they may prefer a written sentence alongside the emoji.
Parents and older relatives are especially likely to send 💐 as a sincere “I am thinking of you and sending beauty.” To them, it can carry more warmth than it does among peers.

warnings.title: Wrong flower for grief
warnings.description: On a loss post or hospice update, 💐 can resemble a celebration bouquet, memorial flower, or funeral arrangement. Send 🌹, 🌷, 🫂, or 🤍 instead.

warnings.title: Too formal for a close friend
warnings.description: A close friend may read 💐 as something reserved for people they barely know. Use 🫂 or 🥺 when you want the support to feel more personal and direct.

seoDescription: What does 💐 mean? It often stands in for flowers you wish you could send, offering warm support, congratulations, or celebration in get-well and wedding texts.

longForm.overview:
The first person to reach for 💐 is often trying to send warmth without making a speech. “Get well soon 💐” is a card you can send after surgery, during a hospital stay, or in a casual recovery wish. The bouquet stands in for flowers you wish you could deliver; it does not claim that you bought or sent a physical gift.

Compared with 🌹 or 🌷, 💐 feels ceremonial. It appears for weddings, anniversaries, Mother’s Day, and formal celebrations, and it is especially familiar in family groups and messages from parents. A parent who writes “Have a great day 💐” may mean “I am thinking of you and sending beauty,” while the same emoji from a friend can feel unexpectedly formal.

The surrounding message changes its meaning. In a get-well note it offers support; in a wedding text it carries flowers without implying that the sender arrived with a present. Two bouquets, 💐💐, emphasize the wish. On a grief post, however, that same celebration shape feels like the wrong flower entirely.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
The basic move is simple: put 💐 after a wish and let it carry the flowers. “Speedy recovery 💐” says more than the emoji alone because the sentence establishes the occasion. The same pattern works for “Hope you’re back soon 💐,” and it can sound caring whether it comes from a close friend, an acquaintance, or a colleague.

It also arrives as a simple congratulation, especially for a wedding or anniversary. Sending 💐💐 is the stronger version: it can mean “I really wish I could send flowers.” In family groups, it often comes from a parent or older relative and carries a straightforward “I’m thinking of you and sending beauty” feeling. Younger friends are less likely to drop it into an ordinary chat without a reason.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Don’t send 💐 on a grief thread, a hospice update, or a loss post. On a modern keyboard it looks like a celebration bouquet, so it can resemble a memorial flower or even “I’m sending flowers to a funeral.” Use 🌹, 🌷, 🫂, or 🤍 when support should remain simple and neutral.

It can also be too formal between close friends, as though you are the kind of person who sends a greeting card instead of speaking plainly. A coworker’s wedding is another awkward spot: 💐 may carry more intimacy than the working relationship can support. Use 🫂 for a close friend and save 🎉 for the coworker’s wedding.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 💐 after a recovery wish, acknowledge the thought rather than treating it like a bare reaction. “Thank you 💐 that means a lot” matches their warmth without adding flowers to the exchange. In a family thread, a simple “love you 💐” can return the same caring feeling.

If the emoji lands on your own wedding or anniversary post, treat it as flowers sent in emoji form, especially when it comes from someone close. If it appears under bad news, ask whether it was meant literally; changing the subject to a get-well message may make the situation worse. When the gesture feels too formal, reply briefly and warmly rather than copying 💐 automatically.

faqs.question: What does 💐 mean from a guy
faqs.answer: It usually means “I am sending you flowers in emoji form,” whether that is a get-well wish, congratulations, or romantic warmth. It is not automatically a sign that he is confessing his feelings.

faqs.question: Is 💐 flirty
faqs.answer: It can be, especially with a partner or someone he is courting, because flowers carry romantic associations. Its meaning still depends on the sentence: “happy anniversary 💐” is more intimate than “congratulations to the couple 💐.”

faqs.question: What does 💐 mean in a get well message
faqs.answer: It means the sender is offering flowers and warm wishes in place of a physical gesture. It works well after “speedy recovery” or “hope you’re back soon.”

faqs.question: Should I send 💐 to someone who is grieving
faqs.answer: No. It can resemble a memorial or funeral arrangement when you meant simple support. Use 🌹, 🌷, 🫂, or 🤍 instead.

conversationExamples.message: congratulations to both of you 💐 hope the whole day is as special as you are
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a warm wedding congratulations that carries flowers without claiming the sender bought a gift. Reply with congratulations and mention a memorable detail from the day.

conversationExamples.message: hope you're back on your feet soon 💐
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is offering professional sympathy after an illness or procedure. A simple “Thanks, I appreciate it” is enough; a hug emoji may feel more personal than the workplace requires.
This is the classic family use: sending beauty and showing that the parent is thinking of you. Respond with affection rather than analyzing the emoji.

conversationExamples.message: happy anniversary 💐 hope we celebrate it properly this year
conversationExamples.interpretation: The bouquet adds romance to an anniversary message, but it can feel formal if the relationship is casual. Answer the sentiment directly and suggest how you want to mark the day.

conversationExamples.message: what a beautiful day 💐 congratulations to you both
conversationExamples.interpretation: This fits a public wedding post, where 💐 functions as a light, warm form of celebration. Add a specific compliment about the couple rather than sending a large emoji stack.
